provenance: Herbert Wolverson, Roguelike Tutorial - In Rust (bfnightly.bracketproductions.com/rustbook/), table of contents fetched 2026-08-15 (two independent fetches agreed; a third fetch during Task 1 confirmed the same 74-item numbering with no discrepancy). A pedagogical sequence for building one ECS roguelike on bracket-lib, not a specification of what a roguelike is: an instrument with known bias, never a standard. Its ordering is a teaching order, and its later sections are one specific game's content design. Verdicts are authored by Hornvale about itself, which is a weaker authority than the blind mapping tropes/tvtropes-2012 used; the anchor discipline is what constrains it, and it constrains `present` least. Coverage measures reach against this catalogue only. Introduction, Contributors and Licensing are unnumbered and excluded from the item list: they carry no capability claim. Building for the Web (id 1) is numbered and included as front-matter about the tutorial's own toolchain, not a world capability. COLOUR, BEFORE ANY NUMBER BELOW LEANS ON IT — and stated from a MEASUREMENT, because this campaign got it wrong four times, the fourth time inside its own correction of the third. COLOUR IS ON BY DEFAULT in the playable path: `cli/src/main.rs:586` selects `Lens::Lantern` for the interactive session, and only `--script` takes `Lens::Off`, deliberately, so committed transcripts stay byte-stable. Measured: `possess --seed 42` then `enter; map` emits 414 escape bytes; the same session outdoors emits 0, and the program prints its own reason above the chart — `0 tinted, 31 withheld (water, a mark, or you)` — because seed 42's flagship stands on water. Seed 13 outdoors reports `30 tinted, 1 withheld`, which is the positive control: the walk band tints when there is ground to tint. WHAT IS UNCONDITIONALLY ABSENT IS PER-ENTITY DISTINCTION, and it fails at the glyph before colour is reached. In the shipped character-grid client's walk band, `clients/game/core/src/chart.rs` draws `@` for the possession and `+` for EVERYTHING ELSE — its own words, 'one glyph for here and one for everything else in view, terrain and marks alike' — so a creature and a boulder are the same character on every seed. No per-entity colour channel exists either: `Mark` carries `noun`/`kind`/`datum`/`salience` and nothing else, and all three renderers withhold tint from a mark by explicit rule. The lesson for a reader, since the truecolor code in `windows/scene/src/surrounds_ascii.rs` will be found again: a code path is not a default, a default is not a screen, and neither is evidence about a particular seed. Say which surface, which seed, and whether the player opted in. Every correction here came from RUNNING the program; none came from reading it.

items.title: Building for the Web
items.anchor: reason:the tutorial's own bracket-lib and wasm-pack build toolchain, not a world capability
items.note: front matter by construction (spec §8): included rather than excluded so the reason travels with it

items.title: Entities and Components
items.note: WEAKEST-HALF, and the render half decides it. SIM half present and richly so: an entity is a ledger subject, its components are the facts committed about it, contradiction-checked against a concept registry no ECS tutorial has an analogue for, and kernel/src/component.rs carries a typed ComponentStore keyed by identity. RENDER half fails AT THE GLYPH, before colour is reached: in the shipped character-grid client's walk band, `clients/game/core/src/chart.rs` draws `@` for the possession and `+` for everything else — its own comment reads "one glyph for here and one for everything else in view, terrain and marks alike" — so a creature and a boulder are the same character, on every seed, with no flag that changes it. An entity is not distinguishable from terrain at all. WHY 0136 CLAUSE 2 DOES NOT RESCUE THIS, since it is the obvious objection: clause 2 protects a single missing ELEMENT inside an otherwise-delivered half, which is what keeps 2.7 `present` with no health bar. Here the half is not otherwise-delivered — what is missing is the whole distinguishability of an entity in the weakest renderer's primary view, which is this chapter's entire deliverable, not one attribute of it. Colour is the SECONDARY point, and it is not a story about defaults at all: colour is ON by default in the interactive path (measured, see provenance), yet no per-entity colour channel exists anywhere (`Mark` carries noun/kind/datum/salience) and all three renderers withhold tint from a mark by explicit rule, so `Renderable { glyph, fg, bg }` has no counterpart in either field. `absent` rather than `refused`, the same conservative direction 4.12-4.15 took: no ratified decision forbids per-entity distinction

items.title: Walking A Map
items.note: `go <dir>` walks the locale mesh and `back` retraces; indoors a wall refuses with a physical reason (the_blocking.rs::a_wall_refuses_with_a_physical_reason)

items.title: A More Interesting Map
items.note: WEAKEST-HALF: sim half present (a sculpted planet rather than a rectangle of rooms and corridors, a pure function of seed and pins, asserted against invariants across a seed sweep). Render half present on GLYPHS ALONE, which is what makes it robust: glyph selection is not lens-gated, so the map reads the same whether or not a cell is tinted, and it does not depend on the seed the way tint does — five relief glyphs `_ . : ^ A` and three water glyphs `~ = +` outdoors, `#`/`.`/`+` for wall, floor and threshold indoors. A player reading an uncoloured terminal still sees the map

items.title: Field of View
items.note: windows/vessel/src/lattice/sight.rs is Ford's SYMMETRIC recursive shadowcasting over four quadrants (sight_is_symmetric is a property test over every ordered floor pair); the walk band carries the remembered-vs-seen half through purview.rs, and The Sighting gates the `sensed` channel on it. The seen/remembered distinction is carried by a GLYPH twin rather than a dimmed tint — `faded()` maps `.`->`,`, `^`->`n`, `&`->`%` — so it survives an uncoloured cell, an uncoloured terminal, and the monochrome client alike

items.title: Monsters
items.note: WEAKEST-HALF: sim half present (derive_npcs_are_distinct_and_placed; a creature beyond sight appears in neither the sensed channel nor the marks). RENDER half, which this anchor cites, and it is a GLYPH claim only: a creature draws as its noun's first letter in the Casement's floor plan, and as `&` in windows/scene's `map` verb, neither of them lens-gated. A creature is never COLOURED on any path — `Mark` carries no colour — so this chapter's `g` and `o` are matched and its red is not. Uneven besides, and this is the same ground 2.1 rests on: in the WALK band neither client draws a distinct creature glyph — `clients/game` draws `+` for a creature exactly as it does for terrain — so only the `map` verb (`&`) and the Casement's chamber-band plan distinguish one. Matches THIS chapter's monsters, which only notice; they do not chase (spec §12), and Hornvale's move only inside `wait`

items.title: Dealing Damage
items.note: no stored, mutable health value may exist anywhere; wounds commit and vitality folds. 0070 closes by ordering combat explicitly after it — combat built first would invent a counter. Not a gap

items.title: User Interface
items.note: was `refused decision:0022`, and that was the asymmetry Nathan caught at G6: the old note ITSELF said "in-repo clients do carry panes" and refused the chapter anyway. Scored on the client: the Quire composes a two-page spread — a plate region (chart or floor plan), an entry region (the sim's narration, wrapped, plus a command line) and an endpaper identity strip — and the Casement carries chart, plan and transcript panes. Two of the tutorial's widgets are missing for INDEPENDENT reasons worth keeping visible: the health bar can never exist (0070), and mouse tooltips exist only in clients/atlas's hit-test readout, not in the game clients

items.title: Items and Inventory
items.note: there is no concept for `object` anywhere in the registry — sword → weapon → tool → artifact → object has no member — so nothing material can be picked up, carried or dropped until the genus exists

items.title: Ranged Scrolls/Targeting
items.note: the chapter's payload is damage at range (magic missile, fireball); 0070 forbids the counter it removes. The scroll half additionally waits on MAT-object-genus, and the targeting UI on 0022 — but the ratified refusal is the load-bearing one

items.title: Saving and Loading
items.note: a world is a seed plus a ledger serialized to JSON; reload re-derives everything else, and entity ids are never reused across a reload. Decision 0007 makes the save tiny by construction

items.title: Delving Deeper
items.note: RE-SCORED, The Gallery: the blocker cited here is resolved, not merely moved. Sim half present, unchanged: `delve`/`climb` descend into and return from the cave at a cell (delve_has_three_distinguishable_outcomes), `dive`/`surface` do the same through the water column, and the place is derived rather than regenerated. RENDER half is now present: the underground band gets its own `SpatialChannel::Underground`/`vessel/level/v1`, the pane and `map` agree on it (the_pane_and_the_verb_agree_underground), and lit/remembered/never-seen are distinguishable by glyph alone. NOT weightless: the pane anchors a level's own extent corner to a fixed-width plate with no camera-follow, so a rung wider than the plate can walk `you` off-screen — registered separately as `MAP-underworld-viewport` rather than folded back into this verdict, since it is a render-quality gap, not an absent chart

items.title: Difficulty
items.note: ARGUABLE. Nothing scales challenge to progress today, and the design argues against a power curve (PLAY-depth-is-spent-not-scored: there is no level). The registry's one difficulty row plans a DERIVED axis — connectivity of the local social graph — which is a different mechanism from depth-weighted spawn tables, not the same one unbuilt

items.title: Equipment
items.note: same blocker as 2.8; CLIENT-coverage-matrix additionally names body-derived equipment slots (morphology decides slots) as the intended shape

items.title: Nice Walls with Bitsets
items.note: was `refused decision:0022`, which was wrong: 0022 ASSIGNS glyph selection to the client, it does not forbid it. Scored on the client, every wall draws `#` in every renderer (lattice/render.rs::WALL, clients/game plan.rs, clients/vessel pane_plan.ts) with no neighbour-bitmask variation anywhere, and no registry row plans one — CLIENT-illumination-deferred plans a richer LAND/WATER/relief vocabulary and CLIENT-glyph-carries-biome a biome one, neither of them walls. A genuine hole

items.title: Bloodstains
items.note: re-anchored from 0022, which assigns residue-drawing to the client rather than forbidding it (MAP-23 already licenses client-side residue). The refusal that actually bites is 0070: there is no blood to draw because there is no damage model to spill it, and 0070 rules that no stored mutable health value may exist anywhere

items.title: Particle Effects
items.note: was `refused decision:0022`. 0022 puts the effect on the CLIENT's side of the line; it does not refuse it — CLIENT-set-pieces calls the ornamental roster "decorative by intent and FREE under decision 0055", which is a licence, not a prohibition. Scored on the client: no in-repo client animates anything (CLIENT-animation-without-a-clock is still raw), so this is planned and unbuilt

items.title: Hunger Clock
items.note: WEAKEST-HALF. Hunger is real and richer than the tutorial's counter — a fold over committed `eaten` facts (hunger_folds_eaten_and_resets_on_a_meal) that integrates faster over a hot occupancy and drives behaviour — but it is a fold over DERIVED NPCs. The chapter is about the PLAYER's clock, and the possession commits no `eaten` fact, carries no drive the session reads, and reaches no screen: `SelfChannel` carries agent/species/settlement/population/room and no vitals at all, so no client can show it. PLAY-host-is-a-narrator names exactly this gap — affect and dread "already computed and all three currently without an honest route to the player"

items.title: Magic Mapping
items.note: the chart today shows only what the possession has walked; knowledge-lit map is designed and unbuilt, and PLAY-inheritance-blocker names the single line (Knowledge::default()) that keeps a vessel from knowing anything it did not see

items.title: REX Paint Menu
items.anchor: reason:REX Paint is a bracket-lib asset format and this is the tutorial's own main-menu art
items.note: toolchain and scaffolding, not a world capability

items.title: Simple Traps
items.note: ARGUABLE. Hazards exist and creatures route around them (danger_routes_a_thirsty_creature_around_a_hazard_to_water), but nothing in Hornvale is CONCEALED, nothing triggers on entry, and no row plans a detection mechanic. Calling this `refused` under 0070 would credit the project with a position on concealment it does not hold

items.title: Refactor Map Building
items.anchor: reason:a refactor of the tutorial's own code organisation into a builder interface
items.note: scaffolding: the chapter adds no world capability, only the seam the following chapters plug into

items.title: Map Building Test Harness
items.note: ARGUABLE. The generator is invocable standalone at a declared BuildDepth and hands its artifacts (terrain, climate) back for inspection with no session anywhere — which is the run half the tutorial's harness exists for. The sweep half is windows/lab (MAP-1, shipped), but its end-to-end run tests are `heavy:`-tiered and #[ignore]d, so citing one would have anchored to a test the gate does not run; the first anchor here, depth_scoped_metrics_match_full_build, evidenced depth-ladder correctness instead. The tutorial's harness also ANIMATES generation inside the game window, which is the half 0022 puts on the client

items.title: BSP Room Dungeons
items.note: windows/vessel/src/lattice/allocate.rs is binary space partition run INVERSELY, and says so against this chapter by name: Wolverson splits a rectangle to invent rooms, Hornvale splits one to allocate space among chambers that already exist, so adjacency is realized by construction

items.title: BSP Interior Design
items.note: a chamber's interior features are derived as an anchor graph and embedded into its cells, faithfully (every_placement_is_faithful) and deterministically — The Hearth's rung 1 of CLIENT-furnishing-ladder

items.title: Cellular Automata Maps
items.note: organic cave chambers DO exist (lattice/grow.rs, Method::Grown) but by region growing with a separation rule, not by cellular automata. The row names CA explicitly as an admissible derivation nobody has built

items.title: Drunkard's Walk Maps
items.note: a builder that is a deterministic function of pins plus noise is admissible; this one is unbuilt

items.title: Mazes and Labyrinths
items.note: no maze generator exists anywhere in the tree

items.title: Diffusion-limited aggregation maps
items.note: unbuilt; the row keeps the technique available

items.title: Add symmetry and brushes to the library
items.note: there is no builder LIBRARY to add primitives to — the two embedders are selected by brief, not composed from brushes

items.title: Voronoi Hive Maps
items.note: weighted Voronoi IS already used, in domains/terrain/src/plates.rs, to partition the sphere into plates whose boundaries become mountains and rifts — but as a tectonic model, never as a builder for walked space. Deferred rather than present for exactly that reason

items.title: Wave Function Collapse
items.note: the row names WFC explicitly as admissible-as-derivation

items.title: Prefabs & Sectionals
items.note: stamping authored map sections is the one thing CLIENT-derived-builders says stays refused — but that refusal lives in a registry row, not a ratified decision, so this cannot be `refused`. Nothing plans it either

items.title: Room Vaults
items.note: same as 4.12. The furnishing patterns The Hearth shipped are RELATIONS (attach/requires), deliberately not stamped geometry (CLIENT-language-not-catalogue)

items.title: Layering/Builder Chaining
items.note: CLIENT-derived-builders names the chain of builders expressing designer intent as the thing that stays refused, and no decision ratifies that; a chain of derivations does not exist either

items.title: Fun With Layers
items.note: applies 4.14's chain; same hole

items.title: Room Builders
items.note: there are two room builders — Method::Rectilinear (BSP) and Method::Grown (region growing) — chosen by the place's own brief, and the checked rules hold across both

items.title: Better Corridors
items.note: there are no corridors to improve: chambers are separated by exactly one wall cell carrying a threshold, so connection is adjacency rather than a carved passage

items.title: Doors
items.note: a doorway derives from a link in the anchor graph, every plan is enclosed and every threshold declared, and `enter`/`out` cross one. A door has no OPEN/CLOSED state and blocks no sight — CLIENT-breach-and-rubble names that gap

items.title: Decouple map size from screen size
items.note: was `refused decision:0022` — a camera IS the client's, which under the weakest-half rule means SCORE THE CLIENT rather than wave the chapter away. clients/atlas carries a full viewport: initialViewport / pan / zoomAt / clampViewport / canvasToTile over a whole-planet scene far larger than any canvas, and the sim's `map out N` gives coarser rungs. The live session's pane is still fixed — CLIENT-snapshot-chart-cannot-zoom — but the capability is in the program twice

items.title: Section 3 Conclusion
items.anchor: reason:a section summary carrying no capability claim
items.note: included rather than excluded so the reason is visible

items.title: Design Document
items.anchor: reason:the tutorial's own game-design document — a process artifact, not a program capability
items.note: Hornvale's equivalents (the Constitution, the spec, the decision log) are process artifacts too, and scoring them here would measure the wrong subject

items.title: Raw Files, Data-Driven Design
items.note: nothing world-facing is loaded from a data file at runtime. Studies and corpora ARE data (decision 0011), but that is the instrument, not the world; the species roster is a Rust table, and everything else is derived from the seed

items.title: Data-Driven Spawn Tables
items.note: ARGUABLE — the DATA-DRIVEN half is exactly why 5.2 is `absent`. What appears at a place is derived from carrying capacity, niche and habitat realm rather than drawn from a weighted table; MAP-encounter-is-a-product plans the refinement that retires wandering-monster tables entirely

items.title: Making the town
items.note: settlements are placed by committed history over a demography fit, never authored; buildings within them carry chambers a possession can enter

items.title: Populating the town
items.note: the roster of who is in a settlement is derived from its population and species mix; `npcs`, `why` and `needs` read them back

items.title: Living bystanders
items.note: bystanders act on homeostatic drives (thirst, hunger, danger) and their movement is observed and recountable — but ONLY inside `wait`: step_with_occupancy has exactly one call site, in Session::wait, so nothing moves while the player walks

items.title: Game Stats
items.note: creatures carry numeric attributes — potency (decision 0064), MindVector's threat_response / deliberation_latency / time_horizon, PerceptionVector, SocietyVector — derived from biology rather than rolled. Two caveats: they are per-SPECIES (PSY-individual-deviation names the missing individual layer), and derived HP is refused by 0070

items.title: Equipment
items.note: the section-4 expansion of 2.13; same blocker

items.title: User Interface
items.note: ARGUABLE. Was `refused decision:0022`. Unlike 2.7 this pass is not about HAVING a UI — it is about the panels this one adds: an attribute block, an equipment list and consumable hotkeys. The blocker is the model, not the renderer: there is no object genus, so the equipment and consumable panels have nothing to display. A reader may prefer `present` on the strength of the spread 2.7 cites

items.title: Into the Woods!
items.note: wilderness regions are classified into twenty-two biomes on a Whittaker diagram over derived temperature and moisture, and species bind to them by affinity — a forest is a place the world produces, not a level builder. Scored on the SIM half plus prose and relief glyphs, deliberately NOT on the atlas viewer's 22-colour palette: the atlas renders a committed scene document rather than a session, so a viewer's palette is the wrong evidence for what a played world shows

items.title: XP
items.note: progression is designed and unbuilt: depth accrues on events rather than duration, is spent rather than scored, and PLAY-depth-is-spent-not-scored is explicit that there is no level

items.title: Backtracking
items.note: there is nothing to persist: a place is a pure function of its address, so returning to it re-derives the same place. The chapter's problem — levels regenerated on re-entry — cannot arise

items.title: Into the caverns
items.note: RE-SCORED, The Gallery: same fix as 2.11, cited separately since a reader may land on either without the other. Sim half present, unchanged: caves are derived under land cells, every passage is traversable in both directions (a_cave_mouth_reaches_at_least_one_chamber), and `delve` reaches them. RENDER half is now present: the underworld has its own chart (`vessel/level/v1`) rather than drawing the surface. Same caveat as 2.11 applies and is not restated in full here: the pane's fixed-width plate has no camera-follow, tracked as `MAP-underworld-viewport`

items.title: Better AI
items.note: ARGUABLE. Behaviour selection is a planner over drives, with foresight, hazard avoidance and give-up conditions — richer than this chapter's mode switch, but NOT player-directed: nothing chases, nothing flees, and creatures act only inside `wait`. The player-facing half is one committed `turned-hostile` fact at a grievance threshold

items.title: Spatial Indexing Revisited
items.note: Occupancy is a per-cell index of who stands where, bubble-only and never serialized (decision 0069); the kernel additionally carries SPO/PSO/OSP permutation indexes over the fact ledger

items.title: Item Stats and Vendors
items.note: objects are the prior blocker; the exchange half is SOC-1's exchange axis and TECH-2's coinage, both unbuilt

items.title: Deep caverns
items.note: RE-SCORED, The Gallery: the OLD blocker (no chart of its own) is cleared, not merely relabelled — MAP-underworld-chart is `shipped` and this item no longer cites it. A NEW, narrower blocker took its place, and it lands hardest on exactly this item's subject. Sim half present, unchanged: a cave's depth is a derived BandKind — Regolith / Cover / Roots / Basement — read out of the stratigraphic column by `cave_depth` (a_strong_process_reaches_one_band_deeper). RENDER half is present but WEAKEST-HALF here specifically: `level::draw` anchors a rung's own extent corner to a fixed-width plate with no camera-follow, and EVERY walkable rung is wider than that plate — the five are ranks 1-5 of the ladder, 44x26 to 60x34, so none of them fits, and the marker can vanish on the FIRST rung rather than only a deep one. A deep cavern is merely where the loss is worst: at an 80x24 terminal a player sees 69.9% of Undercroft down to 39.2% of Nadir, with nothing on screen to say why. Present is not the honest verdict for a chapter about deep caverns specifically; deferred, citing the new row, is

items.title: Cavern to Dwarf Fort
items.note: no settlement is ever placed below the surface: occupation sits on the walk band, and subterranean species get cave carrying capacity without founding anything there. MAP-69 makes surface-versus-underground its own future campaign, dwarven over/under commerce included

items.title: Town Portals
items.note: no fast travel of any kind. CLIENT-coverage-matrix records this as a CLASH rather than a gap — a portal presumes the enter/exit scale seam, which UNI-37 holds deliberately shut — but nothing ratifies that, so it is not `refused`

items.title: Magic Items
items.note: the artifact channel — knowledge carried in an object, whose failure mode is that the instance survives while the recipe does not. Identification is planned as inference (UNI-1), not as a boolean flag

items.title: Effects
items.note: ARGUABLE. The architectural capability — a generic, decoupled channel by which one system's action reaches any target, applied after a frozen read — is decision 0003's trace protocol plus the kernel tick. The chapter's actual payload (damage, healing, confusion) is refused or absent, so this is a verdict about the substrate, not the effects

items.title: Cursed Items
items.note: objects first; the cursed/blessed axis would also want UNI-1's inference-over-a-hidden-ruleset rather than a flag

items.title: Even More Items
items.note: more of what does not exist yet; MAP-19's commonsense ruleset (containers, supporters, parts) is the object-scale model these would sit in

items.title: Magic Spells
items.note: magic is designed at length and unbuilt — productions discovered, accords invented — and MAP-spell-corpus is explicit that a published spell list would calibrate parameters, never audit coverage

items.title: Enter the Dragon
items.note: dragons exist as species and carry a potency (the might order is red, black, white, treant, xorn) — what is refused is the boss FIGHT, which is combat, and 0070 orders combat after a vitality model that does not exist

items.title: Mushrooms
items.note: the chapter's subject is a themed fungal LEVEL — a map generator plus the creatures that belong to it — and Hornvale has no per-level content authoring at all, which is the same reason 5.27 is absent. The roster does carry a sessile detritivore (the shrieker) in a subterranean realm, but the test that would have been cited for it asserts a roster-VACANCY table under decision 0094, which is species coverage and not fungal-level generation: right ingredient, wrong subject, exactly as at 4.10

items.title: More Shrooms
items.note: a second content pass of fungal variants and their effects. Hornvale has no per-level content authoring at all, and the effects half is 5.21's payload

items.title: Ranged Combat
items.note: combat at range is still combat; 0070 governs

items.title: Logging
items.note: was `refused decision:0022`; scored on the client instead. A log DOES reach the player — the Quire's entry pane carries the sim's narration verbatim and the Casement has a transcript — so what this chapter adds beyond that is the COLOURED, WEIGHTED fragment, and CLIENT-prose-carries-no-weight is exactly that gap: "the epistemic ink weights ship on the grid only; prose is uniformly Normal", and `narration` carries a string plus a noun list with no salience signal

items.title: Text Layers
items.note: was `refused decision:0022`. The capability the chapter buys is text composited independently of the map, at its own resolution, and the Casement has it: `casement-panes` holds a `casement-transcript` div and a `casement-mapview` <pre> as two separately-styled surfaces, so prose is not stuck at tile granularity. The Quire reaches the same end differently, blitting a plate region and a prose region into one page. bracket-lib's particular multi-console/with_font mechanism is toolchain, not the capability

items.title: Systems/Dispatch
items.note: a System declares the predicates it reads and writes and the schedule is the topological order of that data-dependency DAG, tie-broken by stable label, with a single-writer check over functional predicates — derived, never serialized

items.title: Dark Elf City 1
items.note: the drow exist as a subterranean people and the possession design repeatedly assumes a Drow City to be admitted to (PLAY-two-gates), but nothing generates a settlement below ground. MAP-69 is where that campaign is banked

items.title: Dark Elf Plaza
items.note: a district-scale set piece inside 5.32's city. The district composer exists one band coarser on the surface (CLIENT-district-patterns), so what is missing is the underground settlement to compose within
